name: Steve Jobs
bio: Steven Paul Jobs was an American business magnate, industrial designer, investor, and media proprietor best known as the co-founder, chairman, and CEO of Apple Inc. Widely recognized as a pioneer of the personal computer revolution and digital music industry, he spearheaded the creation of the Macintosh, iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad. Jobs also acquired and guided Pixar Animation Studios to historic artistic and commercial success.

famousWorks.title: Launch of the original Apple Macintosh computer
Release of Toy Story with Pixar Animation Studios
Introduction of the iPod and iTunes digital ecosystem

faq.q: What products did Steve Jobs revolutionize?
faq.a: Steve Jobs fundamentally transformed personal computing (Macintosh), animated film (Pixar), music (iPod/iTunes), phones (iPhone), and tablet computing (iPad).

faq.q: Where did Steve Jobs deliver his famous 'Stay Hungry, Stay Foolish' speech?
faq.a: He delivered the historic commencement address at Stanford University on June 12, 2005.

name: Warren Buffett
profession: Investor, CEO of Berkshire Hathaway & Philanthropist
bio: Warren Buffett is an American investor, business tycoon, and philanthropist who serves as the chairman and CEO of Berkshire Hathaway. Widely considered one of the most successful investors in human history, his disciplined value-investing philosophy principles and folksy wisdom have made his annual shareholder letters global reading for financiers. Buffett has pledged to donate over 99% of his fortune to philanthropic foundations.

famousWorks.title: Took control of Berkshire Hathaway textile mill
Historic pledge to donate majority of wealth to Gates Foundation
Co-founded The Giving Pledge with Bill & Melinda Gates

awards: Consistently listed among Forbes World's Top 10 Billionaires
Inducted into American Academy of Arts and Sciences

faq.q: What is Warren Buffett's core investing philosophy?
faq.a: He practices value investing, popularized by Benjamin Graham, focusing on buying high-quality companies with durable competitive moats at prices below intrinsic value.
A campaign started in 2010 by Buffett and Bill Gates encouraging billionaires to commit at least half of their wealth to philanthropy.
